The Equipment Engineer reports to the Manager II, Engineering and supports laboratory and production equipment at our Piscataway, NJ facilities. This hands-on role maintains and repairs assigned equipment, improves reliability, and keeps complete records of equipment work.

The engineer performs appropriate preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, and calibration activities internally. OEM and third-party providers are used when specialist tools, qualifications, warranty terms, or capacity require outside service.

Hands-On Maintenance and Repair:

  • Perform scheduled preventive maintenance and appropriate calibration activities on assigned laboratory and production equipment, following approved procedures and documenting results.
  • Diagnose equipment failures, perform hands-on repairs within training and authorization, verify performance, and coordinate return to service with equipment users and Quality as applicable.
  • Support a range of instruments, which may include liquid handlers, automated systems, HPLC systems, centrifuges, thermal cyclers, analyzers, and general laboratory equipment.

  • Determine when work should be outsourced to an OEM or qualified service provider and define the service needed.

  • Develop and improve clear technical procedures and maintenance instructions for assigned equipment.

  • Review work order history for repeat failures, downtime, and recurring costs; investigate causes and recommend improvements to maintenance plans, spares, or vendor support.
  • Perform and document equipment work in accordance with applicable site procedures and Quality requirements.
  • Support equipment-related deviations, root cause investigations, and corrective actions in collaboration with Quality and equipment users.

This position is well suited for a scientist who combines strong wet-lab skills with attention to detail, analytical thinking, and a desire to build technical expertise in emerging RNA and lipid nanoparticle technologies.

1. Chromatography and Analytical Testing

  • Prepare RNA, oligonucleotide, lipid, LNP, antibody, and bioconjugate samples for analytical testing according to established procedures and experimental plans.
  • Perform HPLC/UHPLC analyses using UV and/or charged aerosol detection (CAD), including sample and standard preparation, instrument sequence setup, chromatogram review, peak integration, and initial data assessment.
  • Support chromatographic methods for evaluating RNA purity, lipid identity and purity, lipid composition, residual components, and related product-quality attributes.
  • Assist with preparative chromatography, fraction collection, sample tracking, and evaluation of purification fractions for RNA and related development projects.
  • Support analytical method development, optimization, troubleshooting, and transfer under the guidance of senior scientists and the group lead.

2. LC-MS Characterization

  • Support LC-MS characterization of RNA, oligonucleotides, synthetic cap analogs, and related materials.
  • Assist with characterization of attributes such as molecular identity, capping efficiency, and poly(A) characteristics, as appropriate to the method and project.
  • Perform sample preparation and assist with spectral review, data processing, and interpretation under scientific guidance.
  • Support troubleshooting of sample-preparation, chromatographic, mass-spectrometric, and data-processing issues.
